question: A washing machine is marked at ₹30,000. A customer gets two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is the final price (in ₹) that the customer has to pay?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the successive discount multipliers directly to the Marked Price.

Final Price = MP × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)%

Final Price = 30000 × 80% × 90%

Final Price = 30000 × 0.8 × 0.9 = 21600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹21,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹30,000

First Discount (D₁) = 20%

Second Discount (D₂) = 10%

 Successive Discount Calculation

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = MP − Discount Amount

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 30000 − (20% of 30000)

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 30000 − 6000 = 24000

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 24000 − (10% of 24000)

⇒ Final Selling Price = 24000 − 2400 = 21600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹21,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective single discount is calculated as: [a + b − (a × b) / 100]%.

Marked Price (MP) vs Selling Price (SP)

Discount is exclusively calculated on the Marked Price. It acts as a reduction, resulting in the final Selling Price: SP = MP × (1 − Discount%).

Order Independence

The order in which successive discounts are applied does not affect the final selling price. A 20% discount followed by a 10% discount yields the same final price as a 10% discount followed by a 20% discount.
